//dockerfilePath: Relative to the REPOSITORY ROOT, which is also the build context.
The Dockerfile copies Assets/Scripts/Rules and Assets/StreamingAssets, both of
which live outside server/. So the context has to be the root, and this file
sits at the root so Railway uses the root. Moving either one breaks the build
with a COPY error naming a path that plainly exists.
The previous host's config got this wrong in exactly that way.

//region: US East (Virginia), because Supabase is in AWS us-east-2 (Ohio).
The service defaulted to EU West, which puts the Atlantic between the API and
its database: roughly 85ms per query instead of 10-15. Settlement issues several
queries per request, so that is the difference between a snappy API and a
sluggish one on every single call -- and it would have looked like slow code
Pinned here rather than left as a dashboard setting so it survives the service
being recreated, and so the reason travels with the value.
//ipv6EgressEnabled: Supabase direct connections are IPv6-ONLY on projects created after early 2024.
db.<ref>.supabase.co has an AAAA record and no A record at all, so a container
without IPv6 egress fails instantly with network-unreachable -- which presents
as a health check failing in under two milliseconds, far too fast to look like
a network problem and easy to mistake for a crash.
The fallback, if a platform cannot do IPv6, is Supabase's pooler in SESSION mode
at aws-0-<region>.pooler.supabase.com:5432 with the username postgres.<ref>.
Session mode, not transaction mode on 6543: settlement holds a transaction open
across several statements and takes row locks, which transaction pooling breaks.
